items.title: Louie Bellson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Mel Powell, the piano player with Benny Goodman, used to bring him groceries to keep him alive. I was supposed to go with Mel one day, but Benny had me doing something else.

ctx.x: That’s a masterpiece of orchestration. For me, that is incredible. He started you on the best there is.

Bartok – Bela Bartok – was another one. I missed a chance to meet him when I was with Benny Goodman’s band in 1942. Bela Bartok was still living. He was broke. After writing Concerto for Orchestra and all of the brilliant things, he wound up broke. Mel Powell, the piano player with Benny Goodman, used to bring him groceries to keep him alive. I was supposed to go with Mel one day, but Benny had me doing something else. So I missed the opportunity to meet Bela Bartok. He died in 1945. A genius.

What else were you studying with Mr. Baker. Did he have you work out [of] any books? Obviously he had you look at scores. So did he have you . . .? Because you talk about other people like Gershwin or even – he studied the Schillinger method. Is that something that you worked with as well? Or did you work at the Piston method or any of those?
